carousels.name: Urge surfing - ride the craving instead of fighting it

slides.title: Stop fighting the urge. [[Surf it.]]
slides.sub: The technique therapists use for cravings — and it takes about 10 minutes.

slides.title: Urges are [[waves]]
slides.body: They build, peak, and fade — even if you do nothing. Fighting makes the wave feel bigger. Watching it lets it pass.

slides.title: Notice it in your [[body]]
slides.body: Where do you feel it? Chest, stomach, hands? Name it plainly: "Tight chest. Restless legs." Describing it puts you back in the driver's seat.

slides.title: Breathe [[with]] it
slides.body: Slow breath in for 4, out for 6. Rate the urge 1–10 every minute. Many people are surprised how fast the number drops.

slides.title: Your [[surf]] checklist
slides.note: What number does your urge usually start at? Comment it 👇

slides.title:
Ride the wave.
[[Don't drown in it.]]
slides.lead: Hit the panic button for instant tools that stop urges, right in the moment.

slides.title: Most relapses start with [["I'm bored."]]
slides.sub: The trigger nobody takes seriously — until it gets them.

slides.title: Boredom wants a [[fast]] fix
slides.body: An empty evening feels uncomfortable. Your brain reaches for the quickest hit it remembers — and it remembers this one well.

slides.title: Free time is [[risky]] time
slides.body: Many people say their streak is safest on busy days and most fragile on lazy Sundays. Unplanned time is where the habit lives.

slides.title: Plan the [[empty hours]]
slides.body: You don't need a perfect schedule. You need one thing to do when the evening goes quiet.

slides.title: Your [[boredom]] menu
items: Meet: call a friend, go somewhere public.
Learn: one video, one chapter, one skill.
slides.note: What's on your boredom menu? Share one idea 👇

slides.title:
Fill the gap
[[before the habit does.]]
slides.lead: A step-by-step recovery program with daily actions, so quiet evenings have a plan.

slides.title: Your streak doesn't die on Monday. [[It dies on Saturday.]]
slides.sub: Why weekends are when most guys slip — and how to protect yours.

slides.title: No [[structure]]
slides.body: No work, no schedule, no one expecting you anywhere. The guardrails that held you all week quietly disappear.

slides.title: Late nights, [[later]] mornings
slides.body: Staying up late, sleeping in, lying in bed with your phone. It's the exact setup many people describe before a relapse.

slides.title: The "I [[deserve]] it" mood
slides.body: After a hard week, your brain bargains for a reward. Remind it: a real rest beats a cheap hit.

slides.title: Weekend [[game plan]]
slides.note: Which day is hardest for you? Comment SAT or SUN 👇

slides.title:
Make it to
[[Monday clean.]]
slides.lead: Track your streak, check in with your accountability partner and hit the panic button when it gets hard.

carousels.name: Signs you're healing even if you relapsed

slides.kicker: For anyone who slipped this week
slides.title: You relapsed. But you're [[still healing.]]
slides.sub: 5 signs your progress is real, even if the counter says Day 0.

slides.title: Signs [[1–2]]
items: The gaps are getting longer. Three days used to be hard. Now it's three weeks.
You notice triggers before they hit, not after.

slides.title: Signs [[3–4]]
items: You feel worse after. It used to feel normal. Now it feels wrong — that's growth.
You bounce back faster. One slip doesn't become a lost week anymore.

slides.title: You're [[still here.]]
slides.body: You're reading this. You haven't given up on yourself. That's not nothing. That's the whole game.

slides.title: Progress isn't a [[straight line.]]
slides.body: Most people in recovery describe a zig-zag, not a staircase. Judge the trend, not one bad day.
slides.note: Which sign do you see in yourself? Comment the number 👇

slides.title:
A slip is a step.
[[Not the end.]]
slides.lead: Shame-free progress: journal your patterns, track every streak and see how far you've really come.

carousels.name: Stop obsessing over your streak number

slides.title: Your streak counter might be [[hurting you.]]
slides.sub: Why some people do better when they stop staring at the number.

slides.title: All or [[nothing]]
slides.body: Day 47 feels like everything. Day 0 feels like you lost it all. That pressure makes the "screw it" binge more likely after a slip.

slides.title: The number isn't [[the point]]
slides.body: The point is a life you don't want to escape from. Sleep, friends, goals, confidence — that's the real scoreboard.

slides.title: Track [[more]] than days
slides.body: Urges beaten. Triggers spotted. Hours reclaimed. Good days in a row. These keep counting even after a bad night.

slides.title: A [[healthier]] scoreboard
items: Clean days this month — not just in a row.
Urges you rode out without giving in.
One thing you built with the time you got back.
slides.note: Do streaks motivate you or stress you out? Tell us 👇

slides.title:
Count what
[[actually matters.]]
slides.lead: Streaks, journaling and daily progress tracking — built for shame-free progress.
